items.title: BN-Pas pact signals beginning of Malay-Muslim unity, says Akmal
items.summary: MELAKA: The Melaka election will mark the beginning of a renewed push for Malay-Muslim political unity following a finalised electoral understanding between Barisan Nasional (BN) and Pas. Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh welcomed the agreement, saying it would help realise the Tekad Ummah initiative aimed at uniting Umno and Pas, the country's two major Malay political parties. "Umno Youth is grateful and delighted by BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's announcement of a political understanding between BN and Pas.

items.title: Hold off on trips to France for now, MOHE tells Malaysian students in Europe amid riots
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 22 — All 462 Malaysian students currently pursuing their studies in France are reported to be safe, with none involved or directly affected by the demonstrations and riots occurring in several major cities across the country, including Paris. According to the MOHE, its team – through the Education Attaché Office in Paris, in collaboration with the Foreign Ministry, the Embassy of Malaysia in Paris, and sponsoring agencies – is continuously monitoring the situation to ensure the safety and well-being of the Malaysian students. “To date, there are 462 Malaysian students pursuing their studies in France, and no reports have been received regarding any students being involved or directly affected by the demonstrations and riots taking place in several major cities, including Paris,” the MOHE said in a statement.

items.title: Intern found dead in Port Dickson died from fall from height, police say no foul play
items.summary: PORT DICKSON, Oct 22 — A final-year college student undergoing practical training at a hotel in Lukut was found dead behind an eatery here yesterday. Port Dickson District Police Chief Supt Ahmad Afiq Mohd Adnan said the 21-year-old man was found at 6.05 am after police received an emergency call via the MERS 999 line from a member of the public. “Investigations also found no criminal elements in the case,” he said in a statement yesterday.

items.title: 13,072 doctor posts vacant as of June
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 13,072 doctor posts in the Health Ministry were vacant as of June 30, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said. Meanwhile, Dzulkefly said the Health Ministry recorded 3,510 resignations among permanent and contract medical officers between 2024 and 2026. Of the total, 1,252 were permanent medical officers, while the remaining 2,258 were contract medical officers.

items.title: Classes resume: Kuching international school beefs up security with three police officers after teacher attacked
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 22 — Tunku Putra-HELP (TPH) International School has confirmed that it will immediately enhance its campus security measures, including stationing three ancillary police officers on its grounds, following an incident where a teacher was injured by a student yesterday. “While existing safety measures remain in place, TPH has reviewed its safety protocols and has enhanced security measures in consultation with the relevant authorities. “The school is also exploring more comprehensive, long-term security measures for the campus.

items.title: Tesla profits fall on higher spending as 'Elon Inc.' talk builds
items.summary: NEW YORK: Tesla reported lower third-quarter profits Wednesday as near-trillionaire Elon Musk's electric vehicle maker ramped up huge investments in artificial intelligence and other envelope-pushing technologies. Musk, who leads both companies, declined to offer further details Wednesday. The potential merger – which some have dubbed "Elon Inc." – boosted shares of both companies on Wednesday, lifting Musk's wealth back near US$1 trillion at US$989 billion, according to Forbes' real-time billionaires index.

items.title: MIDA's RM305bil green push puts local firms in the spotlight
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is targeting RM305 billion in green investments by 2030, with a stronger emphasis on ensuring local companies capture a bigger share of the opportunities through higher-value contracts, technology transfer and skilled job creation. Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA) deputy chief executive officer (Investment Development) Zuaida Abdullah said Malaysia had recorded RM45.8 billion in green investments to date, including RM12.5 billion in the renewable energy (RE) sector. Between 2023 and 2025, MIDA approved nearly RM10 billion in renewable energy investments spanning solar, mini-hydro and bioenergy projects, underscoring the country's efforts to expand its clean energy capacity.

items.title: Jobs over cost of living top concern among Perak residents
items.summary: IPOH: Employment opportunities have overtaken the cost of living as the main concern among Perak residents, according to a survey by Institut Darul Ridzuan (IDR). The shift in public priorities could reflect changing expectations of the state government's efforts to improve livelihoods under the Perak Sejahtera 2030 development agenda. IDR chief executive officer Dr Zulqarnain Mohamad said the previous year's survey had identified cost of living as the main concern among respondents.

items.title: From pocket money to cooking: How MOE hopes to make maths less scary
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The Ministry of Education (MOE) plans to strengthen the competencies of mathematics teachers through targeted training and the strategic placement of qualified mathematics teachers. Deputy director of the Science and Mathematics Sector at MOE’s Curriculum Development Division Dr Aszunarni Ayob said that the Mathematics Teacher Competency Standards – developed under the Malaysia Mathematics Education Transformation Plan (RTPMM) 2026-2035 – will allow for training programmes to be tailored to the specific needs and competency levels of individual teachers. Furthermore, several Teacher Education Institutes (IPG) will be designated as centres for mathematics education, focusing on teacher training in this specific domain.

items.title: Meta sued in Australia class action over alleged social media harm to children
items.summary: SYDNEY: A class action lawsuit has been filed in an Australian court against Meta Platforms' Facebook and Instagram, alleging that the social media platforms exposed children to harmful content and kept them hooked through algorithms. The lawsuit, filed in the Federal Court of Australia, the country's second-highest court, by law firm MinterEllison this month, could be the first in Australia to hold social media responsible for harming its users, particularly children and teenagers. Meta agreed in August to pay US$18 billion to settle claims brought by nearly all US states that it had designed social media to addict children.

items.title: Three in 10 couples set on divorce changed their minds after counselling, says Family’s Ministry sec-gen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Thirty per cent of couples who intended to divorce reconciled after undergoing family counselling sessions managed by the National Population and Family Development Board (LPPKN). Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development (KPWKM) secretary-general Datuk Dr Maziah Che Yusoff said the achievement demonstrated that counselling could help couples better understand domestic conflicts and reconsider their decision to separate. She said efforts to strengthen the family institution were central to the National Family Compassion Policy (DKKN) 2026-2030, launched by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on Feb 14.

items.title: Unhealthy air quality hits 16 areas nationwide, Nilai worst affected
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 16 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy air quality as of 8am today. Melaka also registered unhealthy readings, with Bukit Rambai recording 160, Bandaraya Melaka (148) and Alor Gajah (101). APIMS data also showed that 49 other air quality monitoring stations nationwide recorded moderate API readings.

items.title: Ringgit opens higher vs US dollar, major currencies
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar and most major currencies on Thursday as the greenback remained under pressure ahead of next week's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting. At 8am, the ringgit was 4.0780/0835 against the greenback compared with Wednesday's close of 4.0790/0825. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said market sentiment remains cautious ahead of next week's FOMC meeting, with investors closely monitoring inflation.

items.title: Oil rises as US orders diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia amid escalating tensions
items.summary: Brent crude futures rose US$1.29, or 1.2 per cent, to US$110.11 a barrel at 00:34 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude gained 97 cents, or 1 per cent, to US$98.12. The US State Department plans to withdraw family members from a number of other US missions in the region, US officials told Reuters. US crude stocks fell by 3.06 million barrels to 412.5 million barrels last week, the US Energy Information Administration said on Wednesday, compared with analysts' expectations in a Reuters poll for an 820,000-barrel draw.

items.title: At 18, Leesya weighs just 14kg, relies on mother for every need
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: At 18, Khalisah Damia Abd Kadim, known as Leesya, weighs just 14kg and is bedridden due to cerebral palsy. Her mother, Siti Robaah Mohd Munaf, 56, said Leesya, the youngest of six siblings, had appeared healthy at birth. Siti Robaah admitted that she initially struggled to accept her daughter's condition, having hoped that Leesya would grow up without health problems.

items.title: In the Dewan Rakyat today: API accuracy, missing Malaysians in Nepal and GovTech
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The achievements of GovTech Malaysia, the status of Malaysians who remain unreachable following flash floods in Nepal, and the accuracy of Malaysia’s official Air Pollutant Index (API) readings are among the key issues expected to be raised in the Dewan Rakyat today. According to the Order Paper on the Parliament’s official portal, during the Ministers’ Question Time (MQT), Young Syefura Othman (PH-Bentong) will ask the Digital Minister to outline GovTech Malaysia’s achievements in advancing the country’s digital transformation agenda. Meanwhile, Datuk Mohd Suhaimi Abdullah (PN-Langkawi) will ask the Foreign Minister for an update on Malaysians who remain unreachable following flash floods that struck Nepal’s Rasuwa district on Aug 26.

items.title: Nasdaq leads Wall Street gains as SpaceX, Super Micro boost AI sentiment
items.summary: SpaceX shares finished up 7.8 per cent after Elon Musk's rocket and space technology firm posted its first profit as a public company. Elsewhere in earnings, Super Micro shares jumped 9.6 per cent and it was among the S&P 500's top gainers after the AI server maker forecast quarterly revenue and profit margin above Wall Street estimates, signaling that AI demand remained resilient. The report also benefited peers HPE, which rose 3.7 per cent, and Dell, which rose 5.3 per cent.

items.title: Melaka seat deal done: BN takes 21, PAS and allies get seven
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Oct 22 — Barisan Nasional (BN) will contest 21 seats while PAS and its allies will contest seven in next month’s Melaka state election, following the finalisation of negotiations between the parties. “BN will contest using the BN logo. In the 2021 Melaka state election, BN won 21 of the 28 state seats contested, enabling the coalition to form the state government.

items.title: Four injured in BMW-oil tanker crash on Penang Bridge
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Four people were injured when a BMW collided with an oil tanker on the Penang Bridge. Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said the four occupants of the BMW had been taken to hospital by members of the public before firefighters arrived. Twelve firefighters, supported by a fire and rescue vehicle and an emergency medical rescue services unit, were deployed to the scene.

items.title: Teen accused of injuring Kuching teacher no longer active student
items.summary: In a statement yesterday, the school said the student was in police custody pending further investigations. It said the case was being investigated by police and the school would continue to cooperate fully with the relevant authorities. The school said it had immediately activated its emergency response protocols following the incident, with teachers and staff promptly alerting the police and ambulance services.

items.title: Rational investing amidst international conflicts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: International conflicts, geopolitical tensions and economic uncertainty have made stock investing increasingly challenging. Share prices may fluctuate sharply, sometimes in response to events that have little immediate impact on the underlying businesses. Understand the Difference Between Uncertainty and Permanent Damage Stock markets dislike uncertainty.

items.title: Iskandar Malaysia's next test: Turning RM525bil investments into lasting economic gains
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Iskandar Malaysia's next challenge is turning investment into sustainable growth, higher-value jobs and stronger local businesses, industry experts said. Zerin Properties founder and chief executive officer Previndran Singhe said Iskandar Malaysia's investment performance reflected the sustained efforts of the Iskandar Regional Development Authority (IRDA) and the Johor government. However, he said the next phase would be more demanding, as attracting investment alone would not guarantee that Iskandar Malaysia became a compelling place to live, work and build businesses.

items.title: Explainer: Why is Sabah's Pan Borneo Highway lagging behind Sarawak's?
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The toll-free Pan Borneo Highway was envisioned as a major transport link connecting Sabah, Sarawak and Brunei. A total of RM10.547 billion of the RM11.153 billion allocated for Sabah's highway project had been spent, yet the project remains significantly behind schedule. In 2024, former Sabah Works Minister Datuk Shahelmey Yahya said Sarawak had arranged sukuk financing early to ensure sufficient funds for all its Pan Borneo Highway packages.

items.title: HRD Corp rolls out massive procedural overhaul [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Human Resource Development Corporation (HRD Corp) has tightened training grant approvals, stepped up programme verification and strengthened investment safeguards as part of a sweeping reform to address governance weaknesses and restore stakeholder confidence. Since June, training applications must be submitted at least 14 days before a programme begins, ending retrospective approvals and giving HRD Corp more time to scrutinise documents and ensure compliance. Since the 14-day advance application policy took effect, HRD Corp has received 137,460 applications under its HRD Corp Claimable Courses scheme for in-house training and public programmes, an increase of nearly 12 per cent over the same period last year.

items.title: Washington orders US embassy staff, families to leave Saudi Arabia
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The United States has ordered non-essential US embassy staff and their families to leave Saudi Arabia, the State Department said on Wednesday, as the kingdom comes under sustained deadly attacks by Yemen's Houthis. "Iranian-supported Houthis have increasingly engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions," State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott said in a social media post explaining the measure. On Wednesday, the Saudi energy ministry said falling debris from the successful interception of a drone targeting an oil facility had killed two people and injured two others.

items.title: Sisi says Egypt to 'defend Saudi territory' and will not attack Yemen
items.summary: CAIRO: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said on Wednesday that Cairo's proposed military support for Riyadh was intended to "defend Saudi territory and does not include an attack on Yemen". At a government event titled Egypt Forum 2026, Sisi said: "We are talking about defending the land and borders of the kingdom." Egypt's top diplomat Badr Abdelatty and spy chief Hassan Rashad delivered a letter from Sisi to Saudi Arabia's de facto ruler, Mohammed bin Salman, the Saudi Press Agency said.

items.title: French fighter jet crashes during training, two killed
items.summary: PARIS: A French Mirage 2000D fighter jet crashed in northeastern France during a training flight, killing both crew members, officials said on Wednesday. Neither the pilot, aged 27, nor his 44-year-old navigator had time to eject before the aircraft hit the ground, Metz prosecutor David Touvet told AFP on Wednesday evening. The crew comprised "a highly experienced navigator and a young pilot who arrived at the base with all the prerequisites and qualifications needed to fly" a Mirage, air base commander Ludovic Humbert said.

items.title: Nigeria Ebola case matches DR Congo strain
items.summary: LAGOS: The Ebola case detected in Nigeria is the Bundibugyo strain behind a major outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), officials said on Wednesday, marking the spread of the deadly disease to more parts of Africa. The case, detected in a woman diplomat in Nigeria — the first there since the current outbreak in the DRC — has revived memories of a widespread outbreak in 2014 that struck several countries in the region. The patient in Nigeria, Africa's most populous country, travelled from Uganda to the capital, Abuja, on Oct 3, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) said.

items.title: How Malaysians can have enough money after retiring: Moving away from choosing EPF ‘lump sum’ payouts
items.summary: Price said, however, that viewing retirement savings as a “pot of assets” could almost blind people into thinking they have a lot of money, while focusing on it as “income” would provide a “reality check”. Introduce a non-contributory pension, raise the retirement age and increase the EPF withdrawal age (If there is an integrated reform of both private and public pensions) Unlike a defined-contribution retirement savings scheme such as the EPF, where members contribute to their own retirement savings, a non-contributory pension provides retirement benefits without requiring recipients to have made contributions. William Price, a former global pension expert with the World Bank who has also worked with the UK Treasury and UK Pensions Regulator, said Malaysia could raise its retirement age and EPF withdrawal age while introducing a tax-funded pension from age 75.

items.title: Instead of a lump sum EPF withdrawal, how an automatic annuity with opt-out option could work for Malaysians
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Licensed financial planner Rajen Devadason said an insurance annuity scheme like Singapore’s CPF LIFE could also work in Malaysia. Rajen said there might be the risk of a political backlash if access or withdrawals from EPF savings at ages 50, 55 and 60 is changed so one possibility is to keep the same withdrawal rules while using a small portion of EPF savings for an annuity. ILO senior social protection specialist Mariko Ouchi said different countries have different problems which means they would need their own pension solutions.

items.title: As Singaporeans live longer, a look at how they manage their retirement savings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Singapore’s Central Provident Fund Board (CPFB) deputy CEO (services) Wong Yan Jun said Singapore’s CPF — the equivalent of Malaysia’s EPF — had in 1987 introduced a phased withdrawal scheme. The Retirement Sum Scheme (RSS) splits up monthly payouts of a Singaporean’s retirement savings over a fixed duration of 20 years to make it last longer. Singapore in 2007 recognised that more than half of Singaporean men and women would live past 82 and 85 respectively, which led to the 2009 introduction of the national longevity insurance annuity scheme, “CPF Lifelong Income for the Elderly” (CPF LIFE).

items.title: Protests banned in parts of Paris as Macron swipes at Trump
items.summary: PARIS: Police banned protests in parts of Paris on Thursday as France braced for more demonstrations, just days after student and other rallies degenerated into some of the worst street unrest in years. The announcement on Wednesday came after President Emmanuel Macron took an apparent swipe at his US counterpart Donald Trump for exploiting the riots for political advantage in the US midterm election campaign. France has admitted it "lost control" amid the frenzy of street violence that erupted last weekend, when masked youths clashed with police, looted shops and vandalised public buildings.

items.title: eBay to slash 1,000 more jobs, around 9 per cent of workforce
items.summary: NEW YORK: US e-commerce platform eBay will cut about 1,000 jobs, or around 9 per cent of its workforce, a spokesperson told AFP on Wednesday, following an initial round of layoffs in February. eBay had 12,300 employees at the end of 2025, before announcing a first round of layoffs in February affecting 800 jobs. In early May, video game retailer GameStop made an unsolicited takeover offer valuing eBay at US$55.5 billion.

items.title: Trump says fraud investigations make 'very big dent' in overseas scams
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump said on Wednesday his administration had made a "very big dent" in scams by foreign criminal networks that lure Americans into fraudulent investments, focusing on an anti-fraud message ahead of November's midterm elections. Trump, members of his Cabinet and other senior administration officials met at the White House for an event on cybercrime prevention, where FBI Director Kash Patel said his agency had taken down 20 scam compounds worldwide. Trump's family has been heavily involved in soliciting investments in cryptocurrency.

items.title: Trump asks US Supreme Court to allow Big Bend border wall construction
items.summary: NEW YORK: President Donald Trump's administration asked the US Supreme Court on Wednesday to let it proceed with a plan to build a US-Mexico border barrier in a remote region of West Texas that includes Big Bend National Park. The plaintiffs challenged a series of waivers issued by the US Department of Homeland Security to expedite the construction of roads and barriers in the Big Bend region, bypassing various environmental and conservation laws. US District Judge Kathleen Cardone in El Paso issued an injunction on Oct 2 halting construction.

items.title: High cost may make families think twice
items.summary: The East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) offers a competitive alternative to express buses and flights for time-conscious travellers, but families may find the combined ticket costs less attractive, transport experts said. "Even with train fares of RM125 compared with bus fares of RM50-plus, I still think it is worth the money," he said, adding that the service could encourage more travellers to switch to rail. One-way fares from Gombak to KotaSAS start at RM60 for the Transit service and RM68 for the Express service, while fares to Kota Baru start at RM125 (Transit) and RM147 (Express).

items.title: New genus of tiny crustacean discovered in Sipadan cave
items.summary: SEMPORNA: A tiny crustacean found in a submerged cave off Pulau Sipadan has turned out to be from a new species and an entirely new genus. Named Sipadanomolgus dissimilis, the copepod was collected using a light trap inside the marine cave called Turtle Tomb at the world-renowned diving destination. Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia's Associate Professor Dr Azman Abdul Rahim, who led the research, said: "The researchers established an entirely new genus, Sipadanomolgus, as the specimen exhibits a distinct combination of anatomical features that does not fit the existing genera within the family."

items.title: Women hold 34pc of top board seats
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Women account for more than 34.4 per cent of board seats among Malaysia's top 100 publicly listed companies, but the next challenge is ensuring their representation translates into greater influence over corporate strategy and decision-making. The 30% Club Malaysia said corporate leaders must move beyond meeting diversity targets to building boardrooms where women's perspectives help shape business priorities, strengthen governance and drive sustainable growth. Its chair and PwC Malaysia executive chair, Nurul A'in Abdul Latif, said aspiring women directors needed greater access to professional networks, sponsorship and boardroom exposure to prepare them for leadership roles.

items.title: India urged to cease 'use of excessive force' to curb protests
items.summary: WASHINGTON: United Nations experts called on Tuesday for an independent investigation into Indian authorities' conduct in a recent crackdown on protests, where they said demonstrators sustained injuries and some reported being subjected to ill-treatment. Opposition parties and student organisations held protests in recent weeks, demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over a revision of voter lists that they say favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). "Despite the non-violent nature of the assemblies, law enforcement agencies have reportedly deployed force against unarmed students, including lathi charges, and have prevented thousands from joining the protests," the two dozen independent experts said, referring to batons used to break up crowds.

items.title: Axe attack on teacher in Kuching: Student released on police bail
items.summary: KUCHING: A Form Four student arrested over an attack on a female teacher at an international school in Kuching has been released on police bail. Sarawak Acting Sarawak police commissioner Deputy Commissioner Saifullizan Ishak said police were investigating the incident. "Police are investigating and collecting evidence.

items.title: Haze or ship fumes? Maritime experts want closer watch on vessel emissions at Malaysian ports
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Authorities should examine how much ship emissions contribute to air pollution around major ports, particularly during haze episodes originating from Indonesia, says maritime industry expert Datuk Seri Jeyenderan M. Ramasamy. Jeyenderan, the chief executive officer of Maritime Network Sdn Bhd, said Malaysia’s strategic location along the Strait of Malacca, one of the world’s busiest shipping lanes, offered significant opportunities to develop its marine fuel supply sector, but environmental considerations should not be overlooked. The environmental impact of shipping activity deserves closer attention, particularly when transboundary haze affects Malaysia,” he said in a statement.

items.title: Waze ban: MPs ask if WhatsApp, Instagram pose similar security risks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — The government has been urged to provide a detailed explanation of the rationale behind the ban on the use of the Waze navigation app by civil servants, as well as the risk levels associated with other popular applications. Chow Yu Hui (PH-Raub) said that the ban on Waze, over concerns that location data could be exposed to Israel, warranted clarification, particularly regarding how its security risks differed from those of other popular US-owned applications, such as WhatsApp and Instagram. Moreover, the US government supports Israel.

items.title: Sarawak announces two months’ salary aid for state civil servants, RM700 for federal staff
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 21 — The Sarawak government today announced a Special Financial Assistance (BKK) equivalent to two months’ salary for state civil servants, as well as a payment of RM700 for federal civil servants serving in Sarawak. “This assistance is expected to benefit 19,851 Sarawak civil servants, with an estimated expenditure of RM144 million,” he said while concluding the debate on the 2027 State Budget at the State Legislative Assembly sitting here today. For federal civil servants in Sarawak, he announced a one-off payment of RM700.

items.title: No casualties after ceiling collapses at Tengku Ampuan Rahimah Hospital’s emergency dept in Klang
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 21 — No patients or hospital staff were involved in a ceiling collapse incident at the Emergency and Trauma Department of Tengku Ampuan Rahimah Hospital (HTAR) in Klang yesterday, the Selangor State Health Department (JKNS) said. The incident occurred at 7.15pm along the pathway in front of the department’s Blue Zone. The department said it remained committed to prioritising the safety of patients, visitors and healthcare workers.

items.title: Malaysia’s consumer empowerment index rises to 70.36pc from 63.1pc in 2020
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Malaysian consumers’ empowerment level has improved from moderate to high, with the 2025 Consumer Empowerment Index (CEI) recording an overall score of 70.36 per cent, up from 63.1 per cent in 2020. Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said the increase of 7.26 percentage points reflected consumers’ growing knowledge, confidence and ability to make informed decisions and take action to protect their rights. The Purchase Decision domain improved by 7.11 percentage points to 75.91 per cent, while the Financial Literacy domain rose by 3.97 percentage points to 66.47 per cent.

items.title: Selangor ketum raid nets 27 men, including three civil servants
items.summary: SUNGAI BULOH, Oct 21 — Three civil servants were among 27 men detained in a raid on a premises believed to be involved in the sale and processing of ketum leaves and water here today. Commenting further, Zainudin said the premises also offered cough syrup based on customer requests, which is believed to be used for mixing with ketum water. He said the seized materials, including ketum leaves and ketum water, will be handed over for further investigation in collaboration with the Sungai Buloh district police headquarters (IPD).

items.title: Police arrest male student over alleged axe, penknife attack on teacher at Kuching international school
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 21 — A male Form Four student was arrested after he allegedly attacked a female teacher at an international school here, injuring her this morning. Sarawak acting police commissioner DCP Saifullizan Ishak confirmed the incident, that occurred at about 8am, adding that a penknife and a small axe were found. “Further details about the incident will be made by the Kuching district police chief,” he said in a statement today, adding that the student has been released on police bail.

items.title: Malaysia proposes high-level committee with Indonesia to boost creative industry ties
items.summary: JAKARTA, Oct 21 — Malaysia has proposed establishing a cross-ministerial High-Level Committee (HLC) with Indonesia to accelerate bilateral cooperation in the creative industries and creative economy. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said that the committee would facilitate discussions on collaborative initiatives, including those that could be formalised through memoranda of understanding (MoUs) with relevant Indonesian ministries. He said that the proposed mechanism would also help coordinate cooperation across different ministerial portfolios, as areas overseen by Malaysia’s Communications Ministry fell under several ministries in Indonesia, including those responsible for culture, communications and the creative economy.

items.title: Langkawi ferry runs aground off Kuala Perlis, all 251 passengers evacuated
items.summary: KANGAR, Oct 21 — A total of 251 passengers aboard the Express Bahagia 98 (EB98) ferry from Langkawi, which ran aground on a sandbank near the entrance to the Kuala Perlis Passenger Ferry Terminal this morning, were safely evacuated at 2.50 pm today. “The evacuation operation was carried out in collaboration with the Kuala Perlis Marine Police, the Kuala Perlis Fishermen’s Association and Sea Splash Travel Sdn Bhd after two initial attempts to tow the ferry using Feri Kenangan 6 and Langkawi Auto Express 1 failed due to the falling sea level,” he said in a statement today. Norhafiz said the EB98 ferry departed Langkawi at 9.30am before running aground at about 10.35am near Buoy No 1 in Kuala Perlis, when the captain took evasive action to avoid a fishing net stretched across the inbound and outbound shipping channel at Kuala Perlis.

items.title: More than 3,000 attend Selangor Sultan’s Silver Jubilee royal tea reception in Klang
items.summary: KLANG, 21 Oct — The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, graced a Royal Tea Reception with over 3,000 citizens in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee of his reign at Istana Alam Shah here today. The Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor, Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin and the Raja Muda of Selangor, Tengku Amir Shah, were also in attendance. Their Royal Highnesses were welcomed upon arrival by Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari and Selangor State Secretary Datuk Dr Ahmad Fadzli Ahmad Tajuddin.

items.title: Kelantan orders data collection on Myanmar refugees across all districts
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Oct 21 — The Kelantan government has instructed all district officers to collect data on the number and locations of Myanmar refugees throughout the state as a preparatory step to address issues related to the community. State Local Government, Housing, Health and Environment Committee chairman Hilmi Abdullah said that so far, the state government has only received data from the Tanah Merah district, which recorded about 80 families involving more than 300 individuals, in Kampung Padang Guchil, who cultivate betel leaves over an area of two hectares. Commenting on the jurisdiction of the state government, Hilmi said the state’s powers are limited to matters related to land and premises, including illegal encroachment of government land, violations of private land use conditions, and compliance with business licences under the local authority (PBT).

items.title: Police probe alleged axe attack on teacher by 16-year-old boy at Sarawak international school
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 21 — Police are investigating a 16-year-old male student for allegedly attacking a teacher with an axe at an international school here today. Acting Sarawak Police Commissioner DCP Saifullizan Ishak said police received a report of the incident at 8.03am via the MERS 999 emergency line. He said the report alleged that a student had brought firecrackers and used an axe to injure a teacher.

items.title: Haze: Schools in KL, Putrajaya and five states to open tomorrow, outdoor activities suspended
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Schools in the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, as well as in Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka, Pahang, and Penang, will operate as usual tomorrow; however, all outdoor activities have been postponed due to the haze. In Kuala Lumpur, the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur Education Department announced that all educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) will conduct in-person classes as usual, even though all outdoor activities are to be postponed. In Selangor, the State Education Department (JPN) announced that all educational institutions under its purview will operate as usual.

items.title: Immigration Dept raids 19 locations in Janda Baik, detains 65 foreigners
items.summary: BENTONG, Oct 21 — The Malaysian Immigration Department (JIM) raided 19 locations around Janda Baik in a Mega Integrated Operation this morning and detained 65 foreign nationals for various immigration offences. Its deputy director-general (Operations), Datuk Lokman Effendi Ramli, said the operation which began at 10am and covered Kampung Cemeruh, Kampung Ceringin and Kampung Sumsum, was conducted following complaints from residents and media reports about the influx of foreign nationals in the resort area. Lokman Effendi said the integrated operation involved 150 JIM members from Pahang, Kuala Lummpur and the Putrajaya headquarters, in addition to the cooperation of the Road Transport Department (JPJ) and the National Registration Department (JPN).

items.title: Malaysia reviews framework for technical aid to developing countries amid global challenges
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Malaysia’s Foreign Ministry is reviewing ways to strengthen the institutional framework for the country’s international development cooperation to better support developing countries grappling with mounting debt, escalating conflicts and the threat of a widening technological divide. Deputy Foreign Minister Datuk Lukanisman Awang Sauni said the review would draw on insights from a symposium on the Malaysian Technical Cooperation Programme (MTCP), a key instrument of Malaysia’s commitment to developing countries through human capital development, technical assistance and capacity building. Under the 12th Malaysia Plan (2021-2025), he said the MTCP funded 330 capacity-building programmes benefiting 5,609 participants from 144 developing countries, while supporting 87 scholars pursuing tertiary education in Malaysia.

items.title: MCMC records statement of individual over Facebook content allegedly insulting Negeri Sembilan royal institution
items.summary: CYBERJAYA, Oct 21 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has recorded the statement of an individual to assist in an investigation into Facebook content suspected of containing elements insulting the Negeri Sembilan royal institution. In a statement today, MCMC said the action was taken to complete an investigation under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 (Act 588). MCMC is investigating content uploaded through the Facebook account “Che GuBard”, which is suspected of containing elements insulting the Negeri Sembilan royal institution, as well as touching on the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir and members of the Negeri Sembilan royal family.

items.title: Home Ministry: Govt has no plans to amend citizenship law for children born before parents’ marriage registration
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — The government has no plans to amend Section 17 of Part III of the Second Schedule of the Federal Constitution, which governs the citizenship status of children born before their parents’ marriage is legally registered. Deputy Home Minister Datuk Seri Shamsul Anuar Nasarah said the provision remains relevant to ensure that citizenship is determined in accordance with existing laws. For children born before their parents’ marriage is legally registered, Shamsul Anuar said the child’s citizenship status is determined by the citizenship status of the biological mother, in line with Section 17 of Part III of the Second Schedule of the Federal Constitution.

items.title: Home minister: Malaysia, Japan to strengthen cooperation to combat transnational crime
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — Malaysia and Japan are committed to strengthening security cooperation to combat transnational crime through information sharing and investigative collaboration between the Royal Malaysia Police and the National Police Agency (NPA) of Japan. He said the discussions focused on expanding information sharing and strengthening investigative cooperation to combat drug trafficking, cybercrime, online scams and human trafficking. “Transnational crime recognises no national boundaries.

items.title: Sarawak police probe Kuching school incident that left teacher injured
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 21 — Sarawak police are investigating an incident in which a 16-year-old male student allegedly injured a female teacher with an axe at a private school here this morning. Sarawak acting police commissioner Datuk Saifullizan Ishak said police received information about the incident through the MERS 999 emergency line at about 8.03am today, after the Kuching district police headquarters control centre was alerted to a student allegedly carrying firecrackers and injuring a teacher. He said police were conducting a detailed investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and gather relevant evidence.

items.title: PMO confirms civil servants barred from using Waze over Israel data security risks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 21 — The federal government barred all civil servants from using the Waze navigation application over concerns that sensitive official data and users’ personal information could be harvested and exploited by Israel, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) confirmed today. In a statement, the PMO confirmed that Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim ordered an immediate ban across the public sector to safeguard government data and citizens’ movement information. “Sensitive government information and the personal data of the people must be protected from being exploited by the Israeli regime in ways that could compromise national security and sovereignty,” the statement read.
